Monica / team — my quick counsel notes after an initial pass (see attached for annotated PDF):

1) Subprocessors (Section 3.2): Greenline asks for 15 days. Our standard is 30 days. Recommendation: Offer 30 days but add an explicit \"emergency\" clause: immediate notification + service continuity during emergency (e.g., vulnerability remediation, DDoS mitigation). Also include an objection path where Greenline can request mitigation but not an automatic prohibition; carve-outs for specific named vendors (TransCloud) should be handled case-by-case (we can offer to exclude TransCloud in this deal if required but need commercial sign-off).

2) Transfers (Section 6): We accept incorporation of EU SCCs (2021) as primary transfer mechanism. Counsel suggests adding a transfer risk assessment statement and fallback to EU–US Data Privacy Framework (DPF) where applicable; we must confirm that logs in our US observability layer are covered by SCCs or DPF — technical note: logs are pseudonymized and stored in us-east-1 with KMS encryption.

3) Audit rights (Section 8): Greenline requests log access for 90 days. We generally provide SOC2 reports and allow third-party auditors under strict scope & NDA; we do not typically grant direct production access to customer-run auditors. Recommendation: Offer targeted, time-boxed access to relevant logs (30 days) or SOC2 plus a mutual on-site review with limited scope, once per 12 months.

4) Deletion & Certification (Section 10): We can commit to deletion of customer data and provide a certificate of destruction for primary indexes within 60 days of termination; immutable backups are retained per our backup/retention policy but can be scheduled for destruction within contractual windows. Add an explicit carve-out for legal hold.

5) TransCloud (named subprocessor): Ask procurement why this specific exclusion; if it's a showstopper we can propose an alternate vendor or additional contractual safeguards (encryption-at-rest, restricted hashing).

6) Execution method: DocuSign preferred from our side; we can support AdobeSign if they require. Signer order: Greenline legal -> Redwood Legal -> Sales (monica).

Next steps: I'll prepare an annotated response for Monica to send to Anna that includes the suggested language and the options (15-day vs 30-day tradeoff) and commercial impact notes.

Hi Anna — thanks again. Attached is our consolidated response to your redlines (PDF) with counsel annotations. Below are the key callouts and proposed contract language (high level):

- Subprocessors: We propose to keep our standard 30-day notice window. In recognition of Greenline's request we will add an \"Emergency Subprocessor Use\" clause that allows immediate use with post-notification and a right for Greenline to request mitigation measures. If Greenline requires a firm 15-day prior notice, we can consider that in exchange for a limited service credit (to be agreed upon) — please let us know if you want to pursue that trade-off.

Proposed snippet: \"Redwood shall provide written notice of new subprocessors no less than thirty (30) days prior to their engagement. In cases of emergency, Redwood may engage a subprocessor immediately, provided Redwood (i) notifies Customer without undue delay, (ii) documents the emergency basis, and (iii) implements reasonable mitigation measures. Customer may request mitigation steps or temporary suspension of processing by the subprocessor while parties agree on remediation.\" 

- Transfers: We will adopt the EU SCCs (2021) into the DPA and include a transfer assessment summary in the Annex. As appropriate we will rely on the EU–US Data Privacy Framework (DPF) for our US-hosted observability logs; logs are pseudonymized and encrypted with customer-segregated KMS keys where requested.

- Audit rights: We cannot provide unrestricted production access to customer auditors. We propose providing SOC 2 Type II, ISO27001 (if requested), and a targeted, time-boxed log review window of up to 30 days per request. For investigations requiring additional access, we'll accept a mutual NDA and a scoped review facilitated by Redwood's security team.

- Deletion: Redwood will issue a deletion certificate within sixty (60) days for customer primary data upon termination, except where preserved by legal hold. Immutable backups will be expunged in accordance with our backup retention schedule; we will provide a timeline in the Annex.

- TransCloud: We can agree to exclude TransCloud for Greenline as a subprocessor on this account if Greenline requires that exclusion in writing; however, this will require procurement sign-off as it may impact capacity.

Execution preference: DocuSign is preferred (faster turnaround for our legal team), but we will accept AdobeSign if Greenline sends the envelope. Suggested signer order: Greenline Legal -> Redwood Legal -> Monica (Sales).

Please review and advise which thread items are negotiable vs. non-starters. Happy to set a call next week with Naomi on standby.

Best,
Monica Patel
Lead, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147
